_findings.title: Play then immediate Pause throws InvalidStateError out of alphaTab's worklet output
_findings.severity_and_ids_in_plain_words: P0 = must fix before merge. This is one of the two failures making CI red right now.
_findings.the_scenario: You open a drum score and press Play. You change your mind straight away and press Pause -- the two presses less than a second apart. The music does stop, but the page throws an error you never see. On this machine it happens about twice in ten tries; on the CI machine, which is slower, every single time. This is NOT a test-only problem and NOT about the metronome: any person who taps Play then Pause quickly reaches it. Waiting about a quarter of a second hides it completely, which is why nobody noticed until lap 3's new page-error check started listening for uncaught errors.
_findings.whats_wrong: alphaTab 1.8.4's default audio output has no 'has started' flag. AlphaSynthWebAudioOutputBase.play() creates the audio source node but does not start it (alphaTab.core.mjs:24872-24878); AlphaSynthAudioWorkletOutput.play() only reaches source.start(0) INSIDE an async promise, after audioWorklet.addModule() resolves (:41592-41601); and pause() calls source.stop(0) unconditionally (:24880-24885). A Pause arriving before that promise settles stops a node that never started. `playing` in the app flips from AlphaTab's playerStateChanged, which fires independently of that promise, so the button is live during the window. player.outputMode defaults to WebAudioAudioWorklets, so every visitor is on the racy path -- the ScriptProcessor output starts its source synchronously and cannot hit it.
_findings.proposed_fix: Pick Option 1 or Option 2. Either way, file the unguarded source.stop(0) upstream against alphaTab 1.8.4, because the app cannot repair the engine's missing flag. Option 1 is the smaller change and matches the existing NH-335 precedent for tolerating a known engine quirk; Option 2 is the only one that stops a real person seeing the throw.
_findings.why_it_works: Option 1 unblocks the merge and records the debt with a number, so the allowance is removable rather than permanent. Option 2 removes the window itself by never forwarding a pause the output cannot service yet, which is the only remedy that helps users rather than just CI.
_findings.spike_result: MEASURED, and it corrected the reviewers. Run locally on the built app, `--repeat-each=10` per variant: metronome OFF + no gap = 7/10 FAIL; metronome ON + no gap = 3/10 FAIL; metronome ON + ~700 ms gap = 0/10; metronome OFF + ~700 ms gap = 0/10. So THE METRONOME IS INCIDENTAL -- correctness and reliability both framed this as 'metronome on, then play/pause', and that half of their framing is wrong; the immediacy is what causes it. Also: it is 2/10 locally, not the hard 3/3 CI reports -- the CI runner widens the window. Finding #2's fix does NOT help this (still 5/10 with it applied), so the two failures need separate remedies. NEITHER remedy above has been implemented or measured -- Option 1 and Option 2 are both (untested).

_findings.reviewer_why_it_matters: This is the HARD 3-of-3 CI failure at both aa82383a and 62b664f8, and it is now fully diagnosed: it is an upstream alphaTab 1.8.4 race in the DEFAULT audio output, not test noise. `AlphaSynthAudioWorkletOutput.play()` calls `super.play()` (which creates `this.source` but does NOT start it) and only reaches `this.source.start(0)` INSIDE the async `createAlphaSynthAudioWorklet(...).then(...)`. When the synth worker posts `alphaSynth.output.pause` before that promise resolves, `handleWorkerMessage` calls `_output.pause()` -> `super.pause()` -> `this.source.stop(0)` on a never-started node, which throws `InvalidStateError: Failed to execute 'stop' on 'AudioScheduledSourceNode'`. `settings.player.outputMode` defaults to 0 (`WebAudioAudioWorklets`), so every visitor is on the racy output; the ScriptProcessor fallback starts its source synchronously and cannot hit this. A person who presses Play and Pause within the worklet-module fetch window hits it too, and because `super.pause()` throws before `this.source = null`, the deferred `.then()` still runs afterwards and connects an AudioWorkletNode to the destination while the app believes it is paused. The gate is right to fail; what the PR is missing is a decision about it. Adding a narrowly matched ALLOWED entry with a ticket is the project's own established pattern (the NH-335 entry on line 29 does exactly this), and it unblocks CI without weakening the gate for any other message.  [Other reviewers' framings of the same defect: adversarial: Press Play and then Pause quickly and the page throws an uncaught InvalidStateError, no audio plays, and the person gets no message at all — the exact opposite of the error-code promise web/e2e/page-errors.ts cites as its reason to exist. The chain is mechanical: alphaTab's worklet output creates its AudioBufferSourceNode in play() but calls source.start(0) only inside an async .then(), while pause() calls source.stop(0) unconditionally. The transport flips to Pause off playerStateChanged (PlayerShell.tsx:300), which the synth triggers before that .then() resolves, so the second click is reachable during the whole window. Worse, pause() then sets this.source = null, so the pending .then() throws a second time at this.source.connect(...) after having already re-assigned this._worklet — the AudioWorkletNode and its message listener are never disconnected, so each fast Play/Pause leaks one. This is the HARD 3-of-3 CI failure at web/e2e/player.e2e.ts:1271. The defensible fix is to queue the pause rather than forward it: remember that a pause arrived before the output produced its first playerPositionChanged and issue api.pause() then, which the shell already has the bookkeeping for (latestPosition, pendingSeek). || julik-frontend-races: Clicking Play then Pause the instant the tooltip confirms 'Pause' (web/e2e/player.e2e.ts:1297-1299) throws an uncaught `InvalidStateError: Failed to execute 'stop' on 'AudioScheduledSourceNode': cannot call stop without calling start first`, and the PR's own new page-error gate now fails the build on it — CI is red 3 of 3 retries on exactly this case at both aa82383a and 62b664f8. The root cause lives in vendored alphaTab 1.8.4's `AlphaSynthAudioWorkletOutput`: `play()` creates the buffer-source node synchronously but defers `.start(0)` until an async worklet-creation promise resolves, while `pause()` calls `.stop(0)` on that same node unconditionally and immediately. _findings.title: A render between beat mousedown and the first drag move throws on alphaTab's unguarded _selectionEnd.beat
_findings.severity_and_ids_in_plain_words: P0 = must fix before merge. This is the second of the two failures making CI red, and it is the one whose cause two reviewers had MISATTRIBUTED to dropPlaybackSelection.
_findings.the_scenario: You press and hold the mouse on a bar to start selecting a range to loop. Before you move the mouse, the score redraws -- you nudged the window's size, or a setting you changed a moment earlier finished applying. The page throws, and the selection you were starting is broken. The same throw is what makes the test this pull request added for unticking a track flaky: it fails sometimes and passes on retry, which is a weaker guarantee than the regression it was written to pin.
_findings.whats_wrong: alphaTab's _onBeatMouseDown sets _selectionStart = {beat} but leaves _selectionEnd undefined (alphaTab.core.mjs:47626-47627). _onPostRenderFinished then reads this._selectionEnd.beat with no guard (:48220) -- the ONLY unguarded read of that field among all 18 selection-state sites in the bundle. Any render that completes while the pointer is down and before the first move resolves a second beat throws exactly `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'beat')`.
_findings.proposed_fix: Add that one subscription in NotationSurface.tsx. Leave web/lib/alphatab/playback-selection.ts alone -- it was measured correct and is NOT the cause. Also worth filing upstream: _onPostRenderFinished should guard _selectionEnd the way _cursorSelectRange already does.
_findings.why_it_works: alphaTab sets _selectionStart/_selectionEnd before it triggers beatMouseDown, so the seed lands after the engine's own assignment and replaces the undefined half. _onBeatMouseMove overwrites _selectionEnd as soon as the pointer reaches a different beat, so dragging is unchanged, and a pointer that never moves still takes the ordinary single-beat clear on mouse-up.
_findings.spike_result: MEASURED, WITH A CONTROL -- this is the strongest-evidenced item in the lap. The half-set pair {start:true, end:false} was directly observed coming out of _onBeatMouseDown. Forcing a render over that state throws, and the stack is FRAME-FOR-FRAME IDENTICAL to CI's (lh.Dw -> Xs.trigger -> jn.Zu -> Worker.<anonymous>; lh.Dw is _onPostRenderFinished). With the fix applied: the forced mechanism went 20/20 FAIL -> 20/20 PASS, `pnpm typecheck` exited 0 with no cast needed, and THE FULL web e2e SUITE PASSED 88/88. Five named drag-selection cases still pass. The control matters: reverting the fix and rebuilding put it back to 20/20 fail, so the change is the fix and not build or machine timing. Caveat stated plainly: the natural CI case never reproduced locally (0 in 15 stock runs), so the verdict rests on the forced mechanism plus the identical stack, not on a natural failure rate. A resize mid-drag reaches it too, so the untick case is not special.

_findings.reviewer_why_it_matters: This explains the FLAKY `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'beat')` in `unticking the track a bar selection sits on does not throw`, and it is NOT a failure of dropPlaybackSelection — it is a second, different hole in the same engine state that the module's docblock claims to have closed. AlphaTab's `_onBeatMouseDown` sets `_selectionStart = { beat }` and `_selectionEnd = undefined`, and `_onPostRenderFinished` then does `if (this._selectionStart) this.highlightPlaybackRange(this._selectionStart.beat, this._selectionEnd.beat)` — guarded on `_selectionStart` only. So any render that completes between the mouse going down on a beat and the first drag move onto a second beat throws. `selectBars` in the e2e suite (7 call sites) performs exactly that drag across a Playwright round trip, and alphaTab's own throttled container ResizeObserver (`this.container.resize.on(this.uiFacade.throttle(...))`) is a live source of a render landing in that window — which is why the failure is flaky rather than constant. The engine guards `_selectionEnd` everywhere else (`_cursorSelectRange` returns early on `!endBeat`, `applyPlaybackRangeFromHighlight` tests it), so this one site is an upstream oversight, and dropPlaybackSelection cannot help: the problem is a HALF-BUILT pair, not a stale beat. The fix keeps the pair consistent from the moment the drag starts, using the same public lever the module already relies on, and paints nothing because `_cursorSelectRange` early-returns when start and end are the same beat.  [Other reviewers' framings of the same defect: adversarial: Between pressing the pointer down on a beat and the first move that reaches a second beat, alphaTab holds `_selectionStart` set and `_selectionEnd` undefined — and `_onPostRenderFinished` reads `this._selectionEnd.beat` with no guard. Any render that completes inside that window therefore throws exactly the TypeError CI reports at web/e2e/player.e2e.ts:1234, and it is user-reachable, not just lane-reachable: resizing or rotating the window while dragging a bar range re-renders the score mid-drag. _findings.title: The page-error gate asserts synchronously, so a late throw is silently dropped
_findings.severity_and_ids_in_plain_words: P1 = should fix. A detector that can miss is how a red build reports green.
_findings.the_scenario: The page throws right at the end of a test -- from a redraw that was scheduled a frame earlier and lands after the last thing the test waited for. The check that is supposed to catch uncaught errors has already run and already passed. The test goes green on a build that threw. This is not hypothetical: it is why the flaky failure in this very PR reports as flaky instead of as a consistent red.
_findings.whats_wrong: web/e2e/page-errors.ts:51-56 asserts in a plain synchronous afterEach, with no round trip to the browser after the test's last action. The only writer is the async page.on('pageerror') listener, so an error the browser raises at the tail can be pushed into `unexpected` only after the expect has already passed. Work this PR defers to requestAnimationFrame (queueRender / queueMidi) lands a frame after the interaction that scheduled it, and several tests end on exactly such a change.
_findings.proposed_fix: Make the hook async and drain the protocol with one `page.evaluate(() => {})` before asserting, guarded by `page.isClosed()` so a test that closed its own page still fails on its real assertion.
_findings.why_it_works: `page.evaluate` is a full round trip, so any pageerror emitted before it has been delivered by the time the expect runs. The isClosed guard keeps the hook from failing in place of the test's own assertion.
_findings.spike_result: Not run directly. The spike's measurements support it indirectly and strongly: the flaky case passed 15/15 locally while its underlying mechanism was proven to throw on demand, which is the signature of a racy detector rather than an absent bug. Correctness independently flagged the same missing settle step. The proposed drain is (untested) -- worth measuring together with #2, since #2's fix may hide the symptom that would prove this one.

web/e2e/page-errors.ts:11-14 -- 'Deliberately not page.on(pageerror, () => { throw … }): a throw inside an event handler escapes the test's own call stack ... Collect them and assert in afterEach'  -- the collect-and-assert choice is right; the missing piece is the drain

_findings.severity_and_ids_in_plain_words: P2 = fix if straightforward. No user-facing defect; this is a duplication cost. It survived the soft-bucket rule because it is gated_auto with a concrete fix, not an advisory opinion.
_findings.the_scenario: You change how a slider behaves while being dragged -- say it should snap, or stop committing on every pointer move. _findings.why_it_works: It puts one copy of the drag-commit contract next to the component whose contract it is, so a future change to drag behaviour is one edit. Keeping it as a hook rather than a Slider prop avoids touching Scrubber and TempoControl, which this PR does not change.

_findings.title: Font row commits whitespace the validator collapsed, so the engine refuses it
_findings.severity_and_ids_in_plain_words: P2 = fix if straightforward. A real user-visible defect: the value is accepted and then silently does not apply.
_findings.the_scenario: You type a font into a settings row and happen to use a tab, or paste a value with two spaces in it. The row accepts it -- the validator says it is fine -- and then the engine refuses the value, so the text you set silently does not take effect. The restore path does not have this problem, because it collapses runs of whitespace before storing; only the path you type through does not.
_findings.whats_wrong: isFontShorthand judges `draft.trim().split(/\s+/)`, so '12px\tArial' passes. commitText then commits `textDraft.trim()` with the tab still in it (client/src/components/ui/SettingRow/SettingRow.tsx:107). alphaTab's FontParser splits on the literal space only, so the whole thing is consumed as the size and the parse throws 'Missing font list'. This also makes settings-storage.ts:109's own comment wrong about the code: it claims the write path commits exactly what was checked.
_findings.proposed_fix: Normalize once, then validate and commit that same normalized value. Add a SettingRow case feeding a tab-bearing font draft and asserting the space-collapsed string is committed.
_findings.why_it_works: It makes the checked string and the committed string identical, which is what the restore path already does -- so the two paths agree and settings-storage.ts:109's comment becomes true again.
_findings.spike_result: Not run as an experiment, but the mechanism was traced end to end by the validator through alphaTab's FontParser to the actual 'Missing font list' throw. The proposed normalization is (untested).

web/node_modules/@coderline/alphatab/dist/alphaTab.core.mjs:27249 -- `while (endPos < input.length && input.charAt(endPos) !== " ") endPos++;` (FontParser._splitToTokens splits on the literal space only, so a tab never separates tokens) and `throw new Error("Missing font list");` in _fontFamily()

web/lib/alphatab/settings-storage.ts:109-110 -- `// This is the rule the write path adopted for the same reason: commit exactly what was checked.` / `const judged = typeof value === 'string' ? value.trim().replaceAll(/\s+/g, ' ') : value;` — the restore path collapses runs; the write path does not, so the comment's claim is wrong
web/lib/alphatab/live-settings.ts:168-174 -- applyThenPersist's try/catch turns the Font.fromJson throw into onRejected(), which is the E302 toast in PlayerShell.tsx:628

(Error E302)'. The field says yes and the app says no about the same string. `isFontShorthand` judges `draft.trim().split(/\s+/)`, a whitespace-COLLAPSED tokenization, but `commitText` reports `textDraft.trim()`, so the internal tab survives — and alphaTab's FontParser splits on the literal space character only (`while (endPos < input.length && input.charAt(endPos) !== " ") endPos++`), so `12px\tArial` becomes ONE token and `_fontFamily()` throws 'Missing font list'. The restore path already got this right and says the write path did too: settings-storage.ts line 109 reads 'This is the rule the write path adopted for the same reason: commit exactly what was checked' next to `value.trim().replaceAll(/\s+/g, ' ')`. That claim is not true of commitText. Applying the same normalization there makes the committed string equal the one that was validated, which is what both comments already promise.

Add a SettingRow test that a tab-bearing font draft commits the space-collapsed string.
